title: escort follower in slot 0: the leader refresh writes the formation destination every tick, with the eta speed rule, the 50% slowdown and the frustration counter
derivation: The leader (id 102, radius 100, mass 20000) flies at 200 m/s along its forward 0.6, 0, 0.8 (right 0.8, 0, -0.6, up 0, 1, 0) from the origin (constant-velocity). Self (behaviour FORMATION_FORM_UP injected; owner 102, slot 0, desired range 50, speed 320 = maxFlightSpeed, facing the leader's heading) starts 1200 m behind the slot-0 formation point. Rule (b) of the in-tick order: after the leader moved, self's destination is the leader's position plus coordinatesForEscortPosition(slot): the default pattern's offset -2, 0, -1 (oolite-global-prefix.js:165-171) times spacing = leader collision radius x 3 x highPart (highPart = floor(slot / 4) + 1 = 1) = 300 (186-193), rotated into the leader's frame as right x + up y + forward z (quaternion_rotate_vector maps the local axes to right, up and forward), which is (-660.0, 0.0, 120.0) relative to the leader's start position; setEscortDestination: does not reset frustration (ShipEntity.m:2427-2436, 11900-11903, 12029-12044). behaviour_formation_form_up (5002-5047): eta = (distance - desired_range) / flightSpeed; below 5 s with a leader desired_speed = leader speed x (1 + eta x 0.05), else maxFlightSpeed; then eta / 0.51 against slowdownTime = flightSpeed / thrust and flightSpeed above maxFlightSpeed x 0.05 x max_flight_pitch x max_flight_roll cuts desired_speed to 0.5 x flightSpeed. The closed forms use the pre-update flight speed and position of the tick (the previous tick's), the tick's refreshed destination, and a margin of at least 3% to every decision threshold (asserted when this file was written; the reference sits in a limit cycle at the slowdown boundary later in the flight, so only ticks away from it are checked): t1:C(m5 0.280, mS 0.295), t120:B(m5 0.100, mS 0.152), t240:B(m5 0.124, mS 0.128), t360:B(m5 0.146, mS 0.104), t480:B(m5 0.199, mS 0.047). frustration: tick 1 compares the distance with successFactor 0, so it adds dt (fround); from tick 2 the distance shrinks every tick and the counter loses 0.25 dt (fround) per tick until it reaches 0. Closed forms; the escort stays more than 4 x 100 = 400 m from the leader, so no proximity alert is raised.

title: an escort with no leader and a destination whose distance cannot improve posts shipAIFrustrated at the fround-derived tick 1801 and resets
derivation: ownerId 999 names no body, so [self owner] is nil: rule (b) does nothing and the destination stays (5000, 0, 0), exactly abeam on self's right axis at 5000 m. With no leader behaviour_formation_form_up sets desired_speed = maxFlightSpeed (5012-5013), and success_factor = the distance. The pose is chosen so the distance cannot improve in either float width: maxFlightSpeed is the contract's smallest practical positive value 1e-6 (the schema requires a positive speed, so a ship that never moves is not expressible; at 1e-6 m/s the ship moves 8e-9 m per tick, 1.5e-5 m over the run), which is far below one float32 step of 5000 (4.9e-4), the distance is exactly representable in float32, and the destination lies on the right axis, which the pitch fallback rotates about (d_up 0, d_right 1: stick_roll 0, stick_pitch 0.01, 9525-9565), so the ship's motion is perpendicular to the line to the destination and the double distance stays 5000 exactly. A distance that rounded up in float32 would read as an improvement on every tick (the success_factor hazard recorded by plan 14-01). eta = (5000 - 100) / flightSpeed is +Infinity at tick 1 (flightSpeed 0, never NaN) and about 4.9e9 afterwards, never below slowdownTime, so no slowdown applies. frustration adds dt (fround) on every tick (distance < last_distance is false at 5000 against 5000), and the first tick at which the fround-accumulated value exceeds 15 is 1801 (contract item 8); with no leader noteFrustration posts shipAIFrustrated and the counter is set to 0 (5035-5041). The pitch fallback also leaves the heading error to the destination at exactly 90 degrees.
